name: Ethiopian nationalism
summary: Ethiopian nationalism holds that Ethiopians of every ethnic group form one nation with a continuous history from antiquity, whose independence was won at Adwa in 1896 and defended against Italy in 1936. Its defining political position is that the country is indivisible, so it opposes a right of secession and territory drawn along ethnic lines. Its own texts say little about economics, religion, the family or most other themes.
scope: Pan-Ethiopian (civic) nationalism: the imperial state tradition (Menelik II, Haile Selassie: the 1955 constitution, the 1936 League appeal, his speeches), the unity parties of the post-1991 opposition (AAPO, EDUP, AEUP, EZEMA) and Abiy Ahmed's Medemer. It excludes ethnic nationalisms (Oromo, Tigrayan, Amhara), the Derg's Marxism and the Prosperity Party's wider governing programme. Positions held by only one strand (the monarchy, the sacred emperor, the established Orthodox church, parliamentary details of 1955) are not answered for the whole.

sources.title: Revised Constitution of the Empire of Ethiopia (1955), full text
sources.author: Haile Selassie I (promulgated 4 November 1955); text as hosted by crteducazione.org, a mirror of the chilot.me copy
sources.usedFor: The imperial state's founding text: indivisible sovereignty and territory (Art. 1), the Solomonic line (Art. 2), the duty to defend the Empire's integrity by all means (Art. 21, 36), equal protection (Art. 37-38), the tricolour flag (Art. 124), Amharic as official language (Art. 125).

sources.title: Appeal to the League of Nations (Haile Selassie, 1936)
sources.author: Haile Selassie I (Wikisource, Haile Selassie I Press translation)
sources.usedFor: Defence of independence and territorial integrity, collective security under Article 16 (an attack on one member is an attack on all), equality of states.

sources.title: Selected Speeches of H.I.M. Haile Selassie I, 1918-1967 (Ministry of Information, Ethiopia)
sources.author: Haile Selassie I
sources.usedFor: The Emperor's own statements: Ethiopia's thousand-year-old independence, unity of all Ethiopians, opposition to colonial domination, apartheid and racial discrimination on principle.

sources.title: Nobel Lecture: Forging a Durable Peace in the Horn of Africa (Abiy Ahmed, 10 December 2019)
sources.author: Abiy Ahmed Ali (The Nobel Foundation)
sources.usedFor: Medemer as a civic compact; independence kept for thousands of years; Ethiopia's diversity; equal rights and equal justice for all citizens; rejection of the politics of exclusion.

sources.title: Medemer (English edition: the book's Parts One and Two and two parliamentary speeches, unofficial translation by J. Biruk, 2025)
sources.author: Abiy Ahmed Ali (book first published 2019)
sources.usedFor: Abiy's own statements that Tigray is part of Ethiopia and secession is not allowed, that every Ethiopian's death is Ethiopia's loss, Adwa as the proof of coming together, and indigenous solutions drawn from the country's own values. The translation covers only part of the book; the economic and foreign-policy parts are not in it.

sources.title: AEUP calls for annulment of Article 39 (press briefing of the All Ethiopian Unity Party, 9 August 2018)
sources.author: The Reporter (Ethiopia), Neamin Ashenafi
sources.usedFor: A party defending Ethiopian unity asks that the constitution's secession clause be removed and the ethnic federal system amended, saying it endangers territorial integrity.

sources.title: What do party manifestos tell us? (2021 election manifestos of the Prosperity Party, EZEMA and others)
sources.author: The Reporter (Ethiopia)
sources.usedFor: EZEMA: federalism not on ethnic lines, a referendum on amending the constitution; the Prosperity Party: five working languages including Amharic.

sources.title: EPRDF's Nation-Building: Tinkering with convictions and pragmatism
sources.author: Jean-Nicolas Bach, Cadernos de Estudos Africanos 27 (2014)
sources.usedFor: The programmes of AAPO and the Ethiopian Democratic Unity Party (unity of a 'Greater Ethiopia', a unitary state, 'One Nation, One Country', opposition to secession); the nation-building thesis; Adwa as the foundation myth.

sources.title: Nation-building predicament, transition fatigue, and fear of state collapse: an emerging phenomenon in post-2015 Ethiopia
sources.author: Meressa Tsehaye Gebrewahd, Hungarian Journal of African Studies 13(5) (2019)
sources.usedFor: A scholar (Tigrayan, critical of the camp) describing what pan-Ethiopianists hold: citizenship-based nation-building, a unitary or recentralised state, reversal of ethnic federalism, redrawn regional boundaries.

sources.title: The Pitfalls of the Ethiopian Elites' War of Narratives: Part II
sources.author: Shimelis Mulugeta Kene and Solen Feyissa, McGill Centre for Human Rights and Legal Pluralism (2021)
sources.usedFor: The Pan-Ethiopianist camp: Ethiopia as a nation-state, Menelik as state-builder, ethnic federalism as the root of ethnic conflict, a unified Ethiopia albeit a federalist one.

sources.title: Could constitutional reform end Ethiopia's political forever war? (Ethiopia Insight, as reposted by Martin Plaut)
sources.author: Ethiopia Insight
sources.usedFor: Ethiopian and Amhara nationalists as the most vocal opponents of the ethnic federal design; the pan-Ethiopianist case against it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Abiy's own words are that Tigray is part of Ethiopia and secession is not allowed; the unity parties ask to delete Article 39; the 1955 constitution makes territory indivisible and inalienable.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The 1955 constitution makes defending the Empire's integrity with all means a duty of the Emperor, and Abiy says secession is not allowed and describes a law-enforcement campaign against those who attacked the army in Tigray; the AAPO and EDUP stood for a unitary Greater Ethiopia.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The camp holds that regions drawn on ethnic lines are the root of ethnic conflict: EZEMA wants federalism not based on ethnicity, the AEUP wants the system amended, and scholars report pan-Ethiopianists want regions redrawn.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-Ethiopianists reject units built on ethnicity and want regional boundaries redrawn and the effects of ethnic federalism reversed, which is the opposite of merging regions into one unit per people.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Its core claim is that all Ethiopians, of every ethnic group, form one nation: the 1955 constitution makes all subjects the Ethiopian people and Abiy's lecture and book celebrate Ethiopia's diversity and mourn every Ethiopian's death alike.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Abiy calls for equal justice, equal rights and equal opportunities for all citizens, the 1955 constitution guarantees equal protection and no discrimination among subjects, and Haile Selassie abhorred racial discrimination on principle.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Haile Selassie told the African leaders that free men attack and abhor racial discrimination on principle wherever it is found and called for apartheid to be abandoned.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The 1955 constitution ties the throne to an uninterrupted line from Menelik I, Haile Selassie speaks of a thousand-year-old independence, and Abiy says Ethiopians stayed independent for thousands of years.

collective-defense.rationale: Haile Selassie told the League that Article 16 makes every member treat aggression as an act of war against itself, and that collective security is what is at stake.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Haile Selassie condemned the evils of colonial domination of Africans and Abiy's book presents Adwa as the defeat of European colonial pillage; the doctrine's founding victory is against colonial rule.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Resistance to Italy's claim to bring civilization by conquest is the founding experience of the nation, and Haile Selassie opposed colonial domination as an evil, so rule of the 'less advanced' for their improvement contradicts its position.

single-official-language.rationale: The strands differ: the 1955 constitution makes Amharic the official language, while the Prosperity Party's 2021 manifesto proposes five working languages including Amharic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Abiy's book argues that solutions must be drawn from the country's own values and culture, and warns against discarding what is ours.

missingStatements.text: Victory over a colonial invader is the foundation of a nation's unity and identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Adwa (1896) is presented as the founding victory of the Ethiopian nation and the proof of Medemer, coming together, in Abiy's book.

notes: The old audit rested on Wikipedia and one speech; this pass used the 1955 constitution, the 1936 appeal, Haile Selassie's selected speeches, Abiy's Nobel lecture and the translated parts of Medemer, party statements (AEUP, EZEMA, Prosperity Party) and scholarship. Themes searched: government (secession, federalism, regional units, language, legislature), world (collective security, colonialism, alliances, disarmament), society (nation, race, religion, culture), economy (Medemer's economic part is not in the translation and the Prosperity Party programme could not be opened). Imperial-only features (monarchy, sacred ruler, established church) are not answered because the other strands are silent or republican. The Prosperity Party's programme also respects the identity and culture of nations and nationalities, so the camp is not uniform on language; recorded as 0 at low. Most of the old audit's economic and social answers rested on general values or on Abiy's governing record and are null here.
